text: Appendix · architecture and trust boundaries
AT Protocol foundation

Stable identity (DIDs)
Lexicon record schemas
Signed repositories and sync
Memory governance

Authorization and publication history
Reviewed, versioned knowledge
Private Q&A through the gateway
Trust and disclosure limits

Gateway availability and enforcement are trusted dependencies.
Authorized recipients can read and retain copies; revocation cannot recall bytes.
Signed records prove authenticity, not the truth of the content.
Native Spaces and broader delegated execution remain future work.
ADR 0011 · ATProto overview and Spaces alpha in notes
notes:
The selected adapter uses AT Protocol identity, schemas and signed repositories for authenticated publication/distribution. Memory governs reviewed publication, disclosure, authorization, approved recipients/versions, ordering/history and private Q&A. Private questions and answers use Memory’s addressed gateway mailbox. They never enter the PDS, shared publication log, general project timeline or retrieval corpus. The deployment trusts gateway policy enforcement and availability. Authorized administrators/recipients can see plaintext and retain copies; revocation denies subsequent gateway operations; already authorized in-flight work may complete. Previously delivered copies remain readable while local authorization permits and cannot be recalled. Identity signatures do not guarantee factual accuracy. The selected gateway architecture does not depend on experimental native Spaces. Spaces is alpha and broader delegated execution/F2 remains future work.
